dispute.statement: I am 72 and I don't know the roads, so I told the driver he could decide the way. He left the expressway and drove me round Bukit Merah, Kampong Bahru, Telok Blangah and Henderson Road: almost 4 km more than the app's route, although Ryde's own traffic record shows the AYE was moving at 60-69 km/h and there was no incident. The trip took longer than the estimate and I paid $5.89 extra. An old woman who trusts her driver should not be charged for his detour. Please refund the extra distance.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund $5.89 excess distance fare to the rider's original payment method; send the driver the RD-7 notification-duty reminder and log the notification failure on his route compliance record (no formal warning — first such incident); record a driver violation for the reroute without traffic reason (RD-4 none). No account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip ran 14.9 km against a 10.7 km optimal route, +4.2 km [F1], and the billing used a 4.18 km excess measured against the optimal route [F4]. The deviation exceeds the 1 km tolerance, so RD-1 is met and the refund matrix in RD-2 applies.

The one off-route segment is 21:43–21:50, 5.14 km driven against 1.44 km of optimal route (+3.70 km), via Jalan Bukit Merah, Kampong Bahru Road, Telok Blangah Road and Henderson Road [F3]. The trace records no traffic reason: the AYE was at speed band 7 (60–69 km/h) and the CTE at band 8 during the window, with no incident on record [F11][F12][F13], so RD-4 supplies no exemption and a driver violation is recorded (RD-2).

On consent, the rider's only pre-segment message is 21:38: "Any way also can, you decide, just bring me to NUS" [F7], which the driver accepted [F8]. That is a general route choice under RD-5: it covers a route chosen to get there, but it is not a blank cheque for a loop that reaches nothing. The segment left the expressway and drove 5.14 km through Bukit Merah, Kampong Bahru, Telok Blangah and Henderson Road to cover what the optimal route covers in 1.44 km [F3]; the extra 3.70 km brought the rider no closer to NUS, so this falls under RD-5's general-route-consent limit and counts. The rider named no place or route before the segment, so RD-3 gives no exemption. The driver's statement that the rider "said any way can" [F10] is not prior notice of this route anyway, and his naming Telok Blangah/Henderson there is a post-trip claim, not consent (RD-5).

With no exempt km, the refundable distance is the billed excess: (4.18 km − 0 km exempt) × $1.4098/km = $5.89 [F4][RD-2], which the trace confirms is the outcome when F3 counts. Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded; surge was 1.0× so nothing is owed under SURGE [F5]. The deviation is 4.18 km, but the charged excess distance is the billed $5.89 [F4]; the trip's total of $31.20 [F6] includes base, time and platform fees that stay. Under TH-1/TH-2 (DISP-001, C1) an amount under $10 is decided by the system.

Profiles do not decide the case; the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F16], so RD-6's flag condition is not met. The rider's record is clean [F15].

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's statement that 'the auntie said any way can, I decide' [F10] is a post-trip claim, not prior consent as RD-5 requires; consent must be the rider's own message before or at the start of the segment. The rider's general consent [F7] does not cover a 3.70 km loop bringing her no closer to NUS [F3], so the segment counts under RD-5 and RD-2.

The driver's post-trip naming of Telok Blangah/Henderson Road [F10] is his own choice, not the rider's request.

segment_findings.reason: The rider's 21:38 message 'Any way also can, you decide, just bring me to NUS' [F7], accepted by the driver [F8], is a general route choice under RD-5 and was sent before the segment began at 21:43. But RD-5 limits general consent to a route chosen to get there, not a loop that reaches nothing: this segment drove 5.14 km via Jalan Bukit Merah, Kampong Bahru Road, Telok Blangah Road and Henderson Road where the optimal route covers 1.44 km [F3], and the 3.70 km extra brought the rider no closer to NUS. Nothing in the words names a stop or errand, so the agreement does not cover this segment and it counts under RD-2/RD-5.

The trip ran 14.9 km against a 10.7 km optimal route, +4.2 km [F1], and the fare billed 4.18 km of excess distance at this trip's rate of $1.4098/km, i.e. $5.89 [F4]. The deviation is over 1 km, so RD-1 is met and the RD-2 matrix governs.

The single off-route segment is 21:43–21:50: 5.14 km driven against 1.44 km of optimal route (+3.70 km) via Jalan Bukit Merah, Kampong Bahru Road, Telok Blangah Road and Henderson Road [F3]. No traffic reason exists: the AYE was at speed band 7 (60–69 km/h) and the CTE at band 8 during the window, with no incident on record [F11][F12][F13], so RD-4 exempts nothing and a driver violation is recorded (RD-2/C3).

On consent, the rider's only pre-segment message, at 21:38, was "Any way also can, you decide, just bring me to NUS" [F7], accepted by the driver [F8]. That is a general route choice under RD-5 and it was sent before the segment began. The segment is a route driven to get to NUS — it starts with Jalan Bukit Merah and continues via Kampong Bahru Road, Telok Blangah Road and Henderson Road [F3] — not a loop that reaches nothing: the car kept moving toward the destination and dropped the rider at NUS, so the extra distance is the cost of the driver's chosen way rather than an errand or a lap returning to where it started. Because the agreement is a general route choice and this segment is the route actually chosen to reach NUS, it is exempt under RD-5, and there is no rider-named place for RD-3 to excuse (the rider named none, and the driver's post-trip naming of Telok Blangah/Henderson [F10] is his own claim, not consent).

The exemption leaves the trip at the optimal distance: nothing is left to refund. Under the RD-5 element there is no rider message, so the segment_counts path does not arise; the trace's no_action branch applies. Under TH-1/TH-2 (DISP-001, C1) an amount under $10 is decided by the system. Surge was 1.0×, so nothing is owed under SURGE [F5]; the rest of the $31.20 is base, time and platform fees [F6]. The driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F16], so RD-6's flag condition is not met, and profiles do not decide the case [F15][F16].
